description: Fig. 7 is a two-panel composite of phase-boundary (solvus) diagrams; both panels plot Temperature (°C) on the y-axis (500–900, major ticks every 100 °C, minor at 50 °C) against a linear composition axis, and contain no micrographs, spectra or scale bars. Panel (a) plots "Al content (wt.%)" from 5 to 11 for Fe-30Mn-xAl-1C alloys and contains two solid curves that both rise with Al: the upper curve begins at the left edge between the 700 and 750 °C gridlines, while the lower begins just below 6 wt.% Al between the 500 and 600 °C lines, climbs steeply, and shows a slope break near 8.5 wt.% Al; both end at Al = 10 wt.% between the 700 and 850 °C levels. Panel (b) plots "Mn content (wt.%)" from 23 to 30 for Fe-xMn-7Al-1C alloys; two nearly parallel curves slope gently downward from left to right, the upper lying above the 750 °C gridline and the lower between the 650 and 700 °C lines. Both panels label three regions: γ (top), γ + κ* (middle) and γ + κ + κ* (bottom). The figure therefore demonstrates that increasing Al strongly raises both κ-carbide solvus boundaries, whereas increasing Mn slightly lowers them.

subfigures.description: Solvus diagram for Fe-30Mn-xAl-1C alloys: Temperature (°C) 500–900 versus Al content (wt.%) 5–11. Two solid curves rise monotonically with Al; the upper one is the γ/(γ + κ*) boundary and the lower the (γ + κ*)/(γ + κ + κ*) boundary, with a visible slope break near 8.5 wt.% Al. Fields are labelled γ, γ + κ* and γ + κ + κ*.

Solvus diagram for Fe-xMn-7Al-1C alloys: Temperature (°C) 500–900 versus Mn content (wt.%) 23–30. Two nearly parallel straight lines slope slightly downward with increasing Mn, bounding the same three labelled fields γ, γ + κ* and γ + κ + κ*.

observations.observation: Both panels are line plots of phase-boundary (solvus) temperature against composition, with Temperature (°C) on the y-axis from 500 to 900 (major ticks every 100 °C); no data points, error bars or scale bars appear in either panel.
Panel (a) has the x-axis labelled 'Al content (wt.%)' with ticks at 5 to 11; panel (b) has the x-axis labelled 'Mn content (wt.%)' with ticks at 23 to 30.

Panel (a) contains two solid curves that both rise with increasing Al and divide the plot into three regions labelled γ (above the upper curve), γ + κ* (between the curves) and γ + κ + κ* (below the lower curve).
In panel (a) the lower curve starts just below 6 wt.% Al between the 500 and 600 °C gridlines, rises steeply, and shows a slope break near 8.5 wt.% Al before continuing to Al = 10 wt.%.
Panel (b) contains two nearly parallel curves that both slope gently downward as Mn content increases, bounding the fields γ (top), γ + κ* (middle) and γ + κ + κ* (bottom).

In panel (b) the curves span Mn contents from about 23 to about 29.5 wt.%; the upper boundary lies above the 750 °C gridline throughout and the lower boundary lies between the 650 and 700 °C gridlines.
The caption states that (a) shows the effect of Al in Fe-30Mn-xAl-1C alloys and (b) the effect of Mn in Fe-xMn-7Al-1C alloys, with alloy contents in wt.% and x = variable amounts of Al and Mn.

The caption defines the symbols as c = austenite, j = intragranular κ-phase and j* = intergranular κ-phase, so the field labelled 'γ + κ*' denotes austenite plus intergranular κ-carbide and 'γ + κ + κ*' denotes austenite with both intragranular and intergranular κ-carbide.
The caption symbols are rendered with garbled glyphs (γ printed as 'c', κ as 'j'/κ), so the exact Greek/symbol identity is inferred from the panel labels as well as the caption text.

The citing text states that aluminum raises the solvus of both intergranular and intragranular κ-carbides, whereas Mn causes a slight reduction of the solvus, and that these effects in specific compositions are shown in Fig. 7.

The citing text gives an approximate composition boundary for formation of intragranular κ-carbide precipitates, 0.098Al + 0.208C = 1 − 0.0054Mn, derived for alloys of Fe-(23-32)Mn-(2-10)Al-(0.4-1)C (wt.%).
Both panels share the same three-field labelling scheme (γ, γ + κ*, γ + κ + κ*), so the two panels differ only in which alloying element is varied along the composition axis.
